Now speaking

Morning, George — it's Monday the tenth, and the theme of the day is still heat.

Athens is baking again: clear skies, a high around thirty-three, and that dry Meltemi wind pulling the moisture right off you.

Across Europe the heatwave's hitting record territory.

Two quick action items before anything else — those Epic free games vanish Wednesday, so claim them today, and drink water like it's your job.

— personal items —

Let's start with that heat, because it's breaking records across the continent.

Slovakia just hit forty-two point two degrees, a national record, and Italy's put all twenty-seven of its major cities on the top-level red alert at once.

The Danube, Europe's second-longest river, has dropped to record lows — so low that Slovakia's only nuclear plant is throttled back to eighty percent.

It's the fourth big heatwave Europe's had this year, and we're sitting on the warm edge of it.

Meanwhile, the war took an ugly turn overnight.

Ukraine launched a wide drone attack deep into Russia, hitting the border city of Belgorod — five people killed, including a four-year-old, and twenty-nine apartment blocks damaged.

Russia answered with missiles into Kharkiv, striking a high-rise and killing two more.

Ukraine's badly short on Patriot interceptors right now, which is why these barrages keep getting through.

And one for the science file: researchers at UC San Diego ran people through a seven-day meditation retreat and measured real, physical changes — shifts in brain activity, blood chemistry, and immune signaling.

The wild part: when they dripped participants' post-retreat blood plasma onto neurons in a dish, the neurons grew longer branches and made more connections.

Early work, small group, but a striking hint that a week of stillness leaves a biological mark.

On the AI front, there's actually something new.

OpenAI is rolling out what it calls GPT-Live, a full-duplex voice mode you can talk over and that talks back naturally, no more waiting for it to finish, bundled with desktop features that let it drive your computer and juggle agents.

They've also cut prices on the mid-tier GPT models and added a faster mode up top.

Claude Opus 5 is still sitting at number one for raw intelligence, and Google's long-promised top-tier Gemini still hasn't shipped, so treat any launch date you see for it as a rumour until it's actually live.

Weather at home, and it's a proper scorcher.

Clear start to finish: near twenty-seven first thing, a high around thirty-three in the afternoon, and it barely eases to twenty-nine by evening, still around twenty-five overnight.

No rain anywhere.

The Meltemi keeps blowing from the north at roughly seven metres a second, so it'll feel breezy but not cool.

Sunset lands about twenty past eight.

— personal items —

Gaming, and this one's time-sensitive: the Epic Games Store still has Beacon Pines and We Were Here Together free to keep, but only through Wednesday.

Beacon Pines is a lovely, eerie storybook mystery, and We Were Here is a two-player co-op puzzler.

Claim them now even if you play later — once they're yours, they're yours.

Caravan SandWitch is up next from Wednesday.

And your learning bite.

Word of the day: deadpoint — a controlled dynamic move where you catch the hold right at the weightless top of your reach, that split second before gravity pulls you back down.

And an AI tip: after a model gives you an answer, ask it what it got wrong or left out — it'll often catch its own mistakes on the second pass.

That's Monday — hot, quiet, and yours to shape.

Drink water, dodge the sun, and claim those games.
